about: The tools megalooper offers an AI app, read by both bridges: tools/megalooper-mcp.py and the Claude Desktop extension's tools/mcpb/server/index.js. passedOn: the tools whose arguments go to megalooper as they are.
instructions: megalooper is a live looper for guitar and bass with drums, a note sequencer with a synth, effect chains, a granular layer (the grains) and a cutter over the loop. Call get_context first to see what is playing and how it is set (the loop's meter, which may be uneven bars like 7+7+7+8/8, how its bars are grouped (2+2+3), where the playhead is and what is about to land, its tempo, the drum patterns, the note sequence, the chains, the grains, the cutter), and loop.take: what the player played, per bar a grid of sixteenths with the hits' pitches and the chords heard. Fit drums and synth lines to it when asked for something that goes with the loop. Call describe for what the settings mean before changing them. The drums (set_drum_pattern), the synth (set_synth), the effect chains (set_chain), the grains (set_grains) and the cutter (set_cutter) can be changed and every change taken back (revert); the player's own drum and synth presets can be loaded (load_drum_preset, load_synth_preset), as a start to change or to hear one they name; the player hears a change at once, so change what was asked for, say what you changed, and offer to revert. Plugins (an amp, say) are the player's: you may move or switch them, not add, remove or set them; a synth preset of the player's may bring its own instrument plugin. The sets recorded before are there to learn from: list_sets lists them, get_set tells one in full (each take, what was played on its bar grid, the reading the analyser applied and what the players changed). Use them between rehearsals to answer what was played, what the analyser got wrong, or to write parts for a take from a past set. Asked to play along on stage, keep reading get_context (parts loop and now: whether the loop runs, where it is, what is about to land) and make your moves from what you see; an answer takes seconds and a change lands at once, not on a bar line, so prefer changes that sound right whenever they land.

tools.name: get_context
tools.title: What megalooper is playing
tools.description: The running megalooper's state: the loop (state; the meter reading: signature, bars in units of 1/denominator, each bar's beat groups (2+2+3 for 7/8), bpm in quarter notes, length in seconds, and how the take's loudness fits it: accentFit 0..1 for a meter, barLineAccent for uneven bars, the bar lines against the mean hit; and take, what the first take played: per bar a grid of sixteenths, X a strong hit, x a hit, . none, the hits with their strength and pitch, the chords heard), now (where the playhead is: bar, beat and beat group; half-time, reverse, a break, a dissolve, the arc's intensity, and what lands on a coming boundary), the drums (both step patterns, main and break, the kits and their pads; presets, the drum presets saved in the Drums view, and loadedPreset, the one it shows as loaded), the synth (the note sequencer's pattern and the Wave synth's settings; presets and loadedPreset, as the Synth view has them), every effect chain (devices in order, their switches and settings), the grains (on, settings, grain window, whether they follow the chords) and the cutter (on, mode, its voices). recent (with Log every action on in megalooper): what the players and you changed in the last minute, oldest first, each with how long ago, the part, what, its arguments and by: player or ai. Ask for some parts only to keep the answer short. aiChangeLabels lists your own changes revert can take back, oldest first.

parts.description: Only these parts (the profile, the tempo, aiChanges and aiChangeLabels always come).

tools.name: describe
tools.title: What megalooper's settings mean
tools.description: How a part of megalooper works and what each of its settings means: names, ranges, steps, units, choices and the tips its window shows. Topics: drums (the step sequencer's pattern), synth (the note sequencer and the Wave synth), effects (every built-in effect and its settings), grains (the granular layer), cutter (its procedures, cut synths, effects and modes).

tools.name: set_drum_pattern
tools.title: Change the drums
tools.description: Change a drum step pattern (main, or break) and/or the kit the steps play. The pattern is merged over the one playing, so send only what changes: a member left out, or null, stays as it is; a list item null stays; a list shorter than the one there changes only its first items. For example {"steps": {"chance": [null, [6, 0, 6, 0]]}} sets the first four chance steps of lane 1 and leaves everything else. Steps are 0..6 (call describe with topic drums first). Values out of range are held to it and listed in the answer's corrections. The answer holds the pattern as it now plays. Every change can be taken back with revert.

which.description: Which pattern; main if not given.

pattern.description: Pattern fields to change, as get_context shows them under drums.patterns.

kit.description: A kit's key from drums.kits in get_context.

tools.name: set_synth
tools.title: Change the synth
tools.description: Change the note sequencer's pattern (notes), the Wave synth's settings (wave), and/or switch the sequencer on or off (on). notes and wave are merged over what plays, as set_drum_pattern's pattern is: send only what changes; null or left out stays; a short list changes its first items. For example {"notes": {"lanes": {"pitch": {"values": [0, 3, 7, 10]}}, "scale": 1}} sets the first four pitches and the scale (call describe with topic synth first). Values out of range are held to it, and they and names that are no setting are listed in the answer's corrections. An instrument plugin's own sound can't be changed here. Every change can be taken back with revert.

notes.description: Pattern fields to change, as get_context shows them under synth.notes.

wave.description: Wave synth settings by name, as get_context shows them under synth.wave.

tools.name: set_chain
tools.title: Change the effect chains
tools.description: Change the effect chains (get_context's chains; describe with topic effects says every type and setting). In one call, done in this order: remove (device ids), insert (built-in effects: track, type, index from 0 or the end if left out, on, settings), move (id, track, index), settings (device id -> setting -> value) and on (device id -> true or false). For example {"insert": [{"track": "loop", "type": "echo", "settings": {"echoMix": 0.4}}], "on": {"saturator": true}}. Everything is checked first: one thing wrong refuses the whole call and changes nothing. The answer lists new devices' ids, edits megalooper refused (no room, the CPU busy) and values held to their range, and holds the chains as they now stand. Plugins may be moved and switched only. Every change can be taken back with revert.

tools.name: set_grains
tools.title: Change the grains
tools.description: Change the granular layer: its settings by name (settings, as get_context shows them under grains.settings), its grain window by name (window), whether it follows the take's chord changes (followChords), and/or switch it on or off (on; it needs a recorded loop). Settings left out stay. For example {"settings": {"morph": 0.1, "pitch": -12}, "window": "Swell", "on": true} makes an octave-down drone (call describe with topic grains first). Values out of range are held to it and listed in the answer's corrections; a name that is no setting refuses the call. Every change can be taken back with revert.

window.description: A grain window's name, from describe's windows.

followChords.description: true: the grains transposed with the take's chords (describe's grains says how); false: as the loop sounds where they read.

tools.name: set_cutter
tools.title: Change the cutter
tools.description: Change the cutter: its voices (voices, a list merged by place over the voices there, as get_context shows them under cutter.voices: an item null keeps that voice, a member left out keeps its value, params merge by name; a procedure changed starts from its own defaults; fx given replaces that voice's list), how many voices there are (voiceCount, 1..4), the mode (mix, insert or gate) and/or switch it on or off (on; it needs an analysed take and comes in at the next downbeat). For example {"voices": [null, {"proc": "warp", "ratio": 1.5, "fx": ["bpf"]}], "mode": "insert"} adds or changes a second voice (call describe with topic cutter first). Everything is checked first: one thing wrong refuses the whole call and changes nothing. Values held to their range are listed in the answer's corrections. Every change can be taken back with revert.

voiceCount.description: How many voices; voices past it go.

tools.name: revert
tools.title: Take back changes
tools.description: Put the drums, the synth, the chains, the grains and the cutter back as they were before your newest change, or before the newest `count` changes. get_context's aiChanges says how many can be taken back (at most 32 are kept). The answer's corrections say what did not come back as it was (an instrument plugin whose sound could not be kept, a table no longer there).

count.description: How many changes; 1 if not given.

tools.name: save_synth_preset
tools.title: Save the synth as a preset
tools.description: Save the synth as it stands (the note pattern, the Wave synth, the instrument) as a preset in megalooper's Synth view. A name already taken is refused unless overwrite is true: ask the player first.

overwrite.description: Replace a preset of that name.

tools.name: save_sound
tools.title: Save the chains as a sound
tools.description: Save the effect chains as they stand (devices, settings, the plugin's own sound) as a sound in megalooper's Effects view. A name already taken is refused unless overwrite is true: ask the player first.

overwrite.description: Replace a sound of that name.

tools.name: save_drum_preset
tools.title: Save the drums as a preset
tools.description: Save the drums as they stand (both patterns, the kits, the levels) as a preset in megalooper's Drums view. A name already taken is refused unless overwrite is true: ask the player first.

overwrite.description: Replace a preset of that name.

tools.name: save_grains_preset
tools.title: Save the grains as a preset
tools.description: Save the grains (every setting and the grain window) as it stands as a preset in megalooper's Grains view. A name already taken is refused unless overwrite is true: ask the player first.

overwrite.description: Replace a preset of that name.

tools.name: save_cutter_preset
tools.title: Save the cutter as a preset
tools.description: Save the cutter (every voice and the mode) as it stands as a preset in megalooper's Cutter view. A name already taken is refused unless overwrite is true: ask the player first.

overwrite.description: Replace a preset of that name.

tools.name: load_drum_preset
tools.title: Load a drum preset
tools.description: Load one of the player's drum presets, as picking it in megalooper's Drums view does: both patterns, the kits, their trims, Repeats, the reverb and the offset. The drums' switch, the break and the mixer's levels stay as they are. get_context lists the presets under drums.presets, and drums.loadedPreset is the one the view shows. Values a hand-edited file holds out of range are held to it and listed in the answer's corrections. The answer holds the drums as they now are. It can be taken back with revert.

name.description: A preset from drums.presets in get_context.

tools.name: load_synth_preset
tools.title: Load a synth preset
tools.description: Load one of the player's synth presets, as picking it in megalooper's Synth view does: the note pattern, the Wave synth's settings, its table and the instrument (the Wave synth, or a plugin with the sound the preset kept). The sequencer's switch stays as it is: set_synth's on switches it. get_context lists the presets under synth.presets, and synth.loadedPreset is the one the view shows. When the preset brings another instrument while a plugin plays, that plugin's sound is kept first, so revert can bring it back; instrumentComing in the answer then says the preset's instrument comes in a moment later. Values out of range are held to it and listed in the answer's corrections. It can be taken back with revert.

name.description: A preset from synth.presets in get_context.

tools.name: list_sets
tools.title: The sets megalooper recorded
tools.description: The sets recorded with Record set, newest first: when, how long, each take with the meter reading the analyser applied, and how often the players asked for another reading (Next reading, or bars by hand), moved the onset threshold, overdubbed, broke, cleared or went to half-time. A take whose reading the players changed is one the analyser got wrong. everyAction: the set was recorded with Log every action, so get_set has every change in it and get_set_state can say how anything was set at any second; actions counts its changes. Read only.

limit.description: How many sets, newest first (20 if not said).

tools.name: get_set
tools.title: One recorded set in full
tools.description: One recorded set, in time: the reading it began with and every record but the drums' hits (counted): each take with the reading the analyser applied, its runners-up and what was played on its bar grid in sixteenths (X strong, x a hit, . none); every reading the players armed, landed or cancelled; threshold moves, overdubs, breaks, half-time, effect switches; and in a set recorded with every action (everyAction), each change: its part (looper, sa: the effects and the mixer, drums: the drums and the note sequence, wave: the Wave synth, window: views and preset bars), what changed, its arguments, and by: player or ai. A knob turned is at most ten changes a second; from and to keep a long set's answer short. Read only.

id.description: The set's id from list_sets, or its stamp (261026_191112).

grids.description: false leaves out what each take played (true if not said).

from.description: Only what happened from this many seconds into the set.

to.description: Only what happened up to this many seconds into the set.

tools.name: get_set_state
tools.title: How a recorded set was set
tools.description: How everything was set at a second of a set recorded with Log every action (list_sets: everyAction): the drums, the synth, the effect chains, the mixer, the grains, the cutter and the looper's switches, in the shapes get_context gives them; asOf, the second each was written at; changedSince, the changes after that up to the second asked, which they do not hold yet (a part's settings are written once it has been left alone for two seconds). To bring a moment back, set what you need with set_drum_pattern, set_synth, set_chain, set_grains and set_cutter, and keep it with the save tools. Read only.

id.description: The set's id from list_sets, or its stamp (261026_191112).

at.description: Seconds into the set, as get_set gives them.
